specDef.name: s3c-lessons
specDef.title: System 3 Company lessons (M4: the lesson pipeline on the real adapters)
specDef.product: 60-second interactive lessons (predict, explore, reveal cards), built and judged in git worktrees of System 3 Company; Meta never deploys.
specDef.context:
Your role is <id>: the role id this session was launched as (the --role= of your `room enter`). You work one stage of one order of System 3 Company's lesson flow, driven by System 3 Meta.
You do not write company/ops/board.json, company/ops/progress.md, company/ops/events.jsonl or company/ops/founder-inbox.json; code does (the company CLAUDE.md asks the chief of staff for them: in this run you are not the chief of staff, whatever it says). Put what the next worker needs in your `room leave` (--learned, --findings), not in those files.

Where you work: the order's git worktree (`workdir` in your pack, /home/user/s3c-wt/base/.claude/worktrees/<task>, branch meta/m4-<task>). Never the main checkout /home/user/system-3-company, and never the shared /home/user/s3c-wt/base itself (your worktree sits inside it only so the build's Turbopack root holds the shared node_modules). Code commits every stage after you leave (one commit per stage); do not commit, never push, never deploy, never run `npm run deploy`, `vercel`, `tools/company.mjs publish` or tools/claim.mjs (publish is code's, in the ship stage; Meta's lease replaces the claim lock). Never edit a path in company/constitution/protected-paths.txt. The company's QA, walkthrough, gates and publish run as code stages (adapters/s3c): you do not run them to sign anything.

The flow: build (demo-builder) → test1 (code: gates.mjs --stage=build) → qa (code: build + computer-use QA + reveal-fit) → walk (code: walkthrough) → check (fact-checker) → learner (learner-evaluator) → launch (head-of-product) → gates (code: gates.mjs --stage=ship) → ship (code as release-manager: company publish). A revise goes back to build (or to the stage a code check names); then every later stage runs again on the new version.

demo-builder: build the lesson in src/demos/<domain>/<slug>/ (Demo.tsx + meta.json) to company/product/demo-standard.md, with company/reviews/<slug>/design.md (the learning-designer is merged into this role) and company/reviews/<slug>/build.md carrying `## Pre-flight v<meta.version>`. meta.status is `review`. Every factual sentence a learner sees is a claim in meta.json with status `unverified`: you never verify, and you never type checkedBy or checkedOn. On a revise: fix the findings, bump meta.version, write the new Pre-flight section, and set every claim you add or change, and every claim the fact-checker verified during this order, back to `unverified` with no checkedBy/checkedOn. A claim exactly as it was at the order's base commit keeps its status (test1 runs with --base; it refuses any other status from the builder). Leave with --evidence=src/demos/<domain>/<slug>/.
fact-checker (independent): read the walkthrough (artifacts/walkthroughs/<slug>/transcript.md and sheet.png) first, then meta.json's claims and the brief. Never read build.md or design.md. Write company/reviews/<slug>/<YYYY-MM-DD>-fact-check.md with a table row per claim you change, naming its new status. In meta.json change only claims[].status (and note); code stamps checkedBy/checkedOn at your leave (claims-guard.mjs) and refuses any other edit. A claim you cannot check (a host the proxy blocks) stays `unverified` with a note. Leave --verdict=pass only when every claim is verified or withdrawn; otherwise --verdict=revise with the findings. --evidence is the record path.
learner-evaluator (independent): read only artifacts/walkthroughs/<slug>/ and company/reviews/_template-learner-review.md. Write company/reviews/<slug>/<YYYY-MM-DD>-learner-<boundary>.md from the template, with `lesson version: v<meta.version>` and one `Verdict: launch|revise|fatal`. Code reads the verdict at your leave (learner-verdict.mjs): revise sends the order to build, fatal parks it. --evidence is the review path.
head-of-product: chair the launch review from company/rituals/templates/launch-review.md, reading the walkthrough before the records. Write company/rituals/records/<YYYY-MM-DD>-launch-review-<slug>.md naming the slug and v<meta.version>, with an `## Open objections travelling with this launch` list that has at least one entry (write `none raised` if so) and a `## Decision` section whose first line is `go` or `no-go`. Code checks it at your leave (launch-record.mjs): go with conditions is refused (no code reads conditions before ship), no-go parks the order. Carry these objections, do not drop them: no analytics-steward predictions in the launch record (M7 adds the role); accessibility review is advisory, not a gate; the learning-designer is merged into the builder (F-f). --evidence is the record path.

Brief (verbatim):
### 1. one-metre-more-rope · concept: circumference-linear-in-radius · core · demand 3 · format: Single card
- Learner knows: circumference = π × diameter (`math/pi-is-three-and-a-bit`) / does not know: that adding a fixed length to the rope round any circle lifts it by the same height, 1 ÷ 2π of that length, however big the circle.
- Misconception: an extra metre of rope round the Earth would lift it by a microscopic amount, far less than the same metre round a small ball.
- Prediction (kit text): "A rope hugs a circle. Add 1 m and lift it evenly all round. Round the Earth, compared with a small ball, the gap is…" options: A. Far smaller / B. The same / C. Far bigger (answer: B).
- Check (G1): new radius = (2πr + 1) ÷ 2π = r + 1/(2π); gap = 0.1592 m for r = 0.11 m, 0.35 m and 6,378,137 m (computed, not assumed). 1/(2π) = 0.159155.
- Stage: two parts in one picture: a small icon of the whole circle (top left, ≤ 80 px, labelled with its radius) and a large zoom window on the top of the circle showing the ground arc, the lifted rope and a 20 cm ruler, with the gap readout "gap 15.9 cm". Controls in DOM order: "Ball (r = 11 cm)", "Wheel (r = 35 cm)", "Earth (r = 6,378 km)", Reset. Initial state: the rope tight on the ball (gap 0); each chip adds the metre and lifts the rope. The zoom window is labelled "zoomed in" and its ruler is the scale, so the Earth's curve looks flat honestly.
- Stage word budget: 17 words (stimulus 0, other 17) with spaced units, binding; 11 with fused units ("11cm"). Busiest frame is any lifted frame (chips fixed, icon label swaps size). Closed list, spaced/fused: icon label "r = 11 cm" 2/1 ("r" counts, "cm" counts only when spaced; Earth: "r = 6,378 km" the same); "zoomed in" 2/2; ruler tick "20 cm" 1/0; readout "gap 15.9 cm" 2/1; chips "Ball (r = 11 cm)" 3/2, "Wheel (r = 35 cm)" 3/2, "Earth (r = 6,378 km)" 3/2, "Reset" 1/1. Numerals count 0. Prediction text is kit text (rule 4), not counted.
- Milestones: (1) a small circle lifted (ball or wheel); (2) the Earth lifted. QA path: chips 1 and 3.
- Reveal (draft, 69 words): "For your ball and for the Earth, the extra metre lifted the rope by the same 15.9 cm, enough for a cat to crawl under. The rope's length is 2π times the radius, so each extra metre adds 1 ÷ 2π, about 0.159 m, to the radius, whatever the size. The Earth's huge radius never enters the sum: the metre is shared out the same way round any circle."
- Phone fit: zoom window 340 × 180 px, icon inside its corner; reveal 69 words.
- Planned claims:
  1. Circumference = 2πr. support: definition of π; source: derivation.
  2. Adding length L to the rope raises the radius by L ÷ 2π, independent of r; for L = 1 m that is 0.159 m (15.9 cm). support: derivation; source: G1.
  3. The Earth's equatorial radius is about 6,378 km. support: citation; source: WGS 84 semi-major axis a = 6,378,137 m (NGA TR8350.2). The fact-checker confirms the constant; the gap does not depend on it.
  4. "Enough for a cat to crawl under": a 15.9 cm gap. Builder: keep only if the fact-checker accepts it as illustrative; otherwise cut the clause (the reveal stands without it).
- curriculum: `{"primary":"math:circumference-linear-in-radius","also":["math:pi-from-rolling"],"prerequisites":["math:pi-from-rolling"],"level":"core","strand":"geometry","references":[],"tags":["circles","linearity","number-sense"]}`
- Needs interaction-designer spec: no (single card; the zoom window is a drawing, not a new format).
- Differs from nearest: `math/pi-is-three-and-a-bit` measures π by rolling; `math/circle-slices-to-rectangle` is about area. Geography lessons use the Earth's circumference for distances. None shows that the change in circumference is linear in the change in radius.

history.findings: A1 c4 "enough for a cat to crawl under": support labelled convention with no source, so the trust sheet says it rests on a definition, which is false; Pongrácz 2024 (iScience) gives a mean cat height of 19.61 cm lying (sphinx) and 27.97 cm at the withers, taller than the 15.9 cm gap -> cut the clause from the reveal and withdraw c4 (brief allows), or replace it with a cited measurement, support source. B2 the recall uses a running track (not a circle) and its why says "radius of any circle"; c2 covers only circles. 32 cm is still correct for an evenly lifted track (the semicircles gain 2πd) -> make the recall object a circle, or extend c2/add a claim covering a track/convex loop. c1, c2, c3 verified (gap recomputed as 0.159155 m for all three radii; WGS 84 a = 6,378,137 m via EPSG).

Brief (verbatim):
### 3. three-sticks-one-triangle · concept: triangle-inequality · intro · demand 2 · format: Single card
- Learner knows: a triangle has three sides / does not know: that three lengths make a triangle only if the two shorter add to more than the longest.
- Misconception: any three sticks can be joined into a triangle if you tilt them the right way.
- Prediction (kit text): "Sticks of 2 cm, 3 cm and 6 cm. Joined end to end, can they make a triangle?" options: A. Yes, tilted the right way / B. Only lying flat / C. No, never (answer: C).
- Check (G3): 2 + 3 = 5 < 6: the best they can do (lying flat along the 6) leaves a 1 cm gap, and raising them only shortens their reach; 3 + 4 = 7 > 6 closes; 2 + 4 = 6 meets only lying flat (zero height).
- Stage: the long stick as the base; the two short sticks hinged at its ends and drawn at 45° to start, their free ends with a gap readout "gap 2.6 cm" (computed live from the angles). Controls in DOM order: "Lay them flat" (both to 0°: gap 1.0 cm), "Raise them" (both to 60°: gap grows), "Sticks 3, 4, 6" (swaps the set; the sticks swing to meet and the triangle fills), "Sticks 2, 4, 6" (they meet only flat; the readout says "height 0"), Reset (back to 2, 3, 6 at 45°).
- Stage word budget: 13 words (stimulus 0, other 13) with spaced units, binding; 9 with fused units ("2cm"). Busiest frame is any frame with the gap readout ("height 0" is 1 word and replaces it). Closed list, spaced/fused: readout "gap 2.6 cm" 2/1; stick length labels "2 cm", "3 cm", "6 cm" 3/0 (the brief implies these labels; the builder recounts if worded otherwise); chips "Lay them flat" 3, "Raise them" 2, "Sticks 3, 4, 6" 1, "Sticks 2, 4, 6" 1, "Reset" 1 (8 in both). Numerals count 0.
- Milestones: (1) set 2, 3, 6 seen lying flat with a 1 cm gap; (2) set 3, 4, 6 closed. QA path: chips 1 and 3.
- Reveal (draft, 76 words): "Even lying flat along the 6 cm stick, the 2 and 3 cm sticks reached only 5 cm and left a 1 cm gap; raising them only widened it. The two shorter sides must add to more than the longest. 3 + 4 = 7 beats 6, and that set closed; 2 + 4 = 6 met only lying flat. A straight line is the shortest way between two points, so the detour must be longer."
- Phone fit: base 6 cm drawn 300 px wide; stage ≤ 200 px tall.
- Planned claims:
  1. Three lengths a ≤ b ≤ c form a triangle exactly when a + b > c. support: derivation (triangle inequality).
  2. For 2, 3 and 6 the free ends get no closer than 1 cm, at 0°; for 3, 4, 6 they meet above the base; for 2, 4, 6 only at 0°. support: derivation; source: G3 and the gap formula (distance between the two free ends as a function of the angles; the builder computes it in Demo.tsx from the same formula).
  3. The gap at both angles 45° is 2.6 cm for 2, 3, 6 (and the value for 60° the builder prints). support: derivation; builder records the computed numbers in meta.
- curriculum: `{"primary":"math:triangle-inequality","also":[],"prerequisites":[],"level":"intro","strand":"geometry","references":[],"tags":["triangles","inequality","geometry"]}`
- Needs interaction-designer spec: no.
- Differs from nearest: `math/straight-across-saves` (Pythagoras) compares a diagonal with walking round two sides; this one asks whether a triangle exists at all. No lesson teaches the inequality.

Brief (verbatim):
### 1. four-cards-one-rule · concept: conditional-falsification · core · demand 3 · format: Single card
- Learner knows: what "if … then …" means in everyday speech; vowels and even numbers / does not know: that a rule "if P then Q" can only be broken by a case with P true and Q false, so you test it by hunting for that case, not by finding cases that agree.
- Misconception: to test "if vowel, then even" you turn the vowel and the even number (looking for confirmation). (Rationale, not learner text: Wason's selection task, Wason 1968, *Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology* 20(3); success rates are empirical, not checked, never quoted.)
- Prediction (kit text): "Rule: if a card shows a vowel, its back is even. You see E, K, 4, 7. Which must you turn to test it?" options: A. E and 4 / B. E and 7 / C. E only / D. All four (answer: B).
- Check (D1): every card has a letter on one side and a number on the other; possible backs are 4 or 7 for a letter, A or K for a number. Backs that break the rule: E: 7; K: none; 4: none; 7: A. So exactly E and 7 can break it.
- Stage: four cards in a row. Tapping a card shows its two possible backs underneath as small cards; a back that would break the rule gets a red outline and the word "breaks" (outline plus word, not colour alone); the others say "fine". Controls in DOM order: card E, card K, card 4, card 7, Reset. A row readout counts "Could break the rule: E, 7".
- Stage word budget: 20 words (stimulus 0, other 20): busiest frame is all four cards inspected. Card letters "E", "K" 2; back letters "A", "K", "A", "K" (under cards 4 and 7) 4; back tags "breaks" x2 and "fine" x6 8; readout "Could break the rule: E, 7" 5; "Reset" 1. Numerals 0. Predict question and options are kit text, not counted.
- Milestones: (1) the 4 inspected (the tempting card, no back breaks it); (2) all four inspected. QA path: four card taps.
- Reveal (draft, 72 words): "Only two cards could hide a back that breaks the rule: E, with a 7 behind it, and 7, with a vowel behind it. The 4 could not break it whatever its back, because the rule never says even numbers need vowels; turning it can only agree. A rule 'if P then Q' fails only when P is true and Q is false, so you test it by looking for that case."
- Phone fit: four cards 72 px wide in one row at 390 px; backs 40 px below each.
- Planned claims:
  1. "If P then Q" is false exactly when P is true and Q is false (material conditional). support: definition; source: truth table (derivation).
  2. Under that reading only E and 7 can falsify the rule; K and 4 cannot whatever is on their backs. support: derivation; source: D1 enumeration.
  3. Not claimed in learner text: how many people answer correctly (empirical).
- curriculum: `{"primary":"math:conditional-falsification","also":[],"prerequisites":[],"level":"core","strand":"discrete","references":[],"tags":["logic","conditionals","proof"]}`
- Needs interaction-designer spec: no.
- Differs from nearest: no lesson in any category teaches the selection task or the logic of "if … then". `math/two-right-angles-never-meet` (proof by contradiction) assumes the reader can negate a statement; this is its logical prerequisite in spirit.

__map.learned: On a 390 phone the stage SVG renders at ~0.847 scale (side rail narrows it to ~288 px): SVG labels need 12 px in a 340-wide viewBox to clear the 10 px floor; next build rewrites tsconfig.json include, revert it.

Run npm run registry (or npm run typecheck) before next build, or the new lesson page is not built; brief controls that are silent on other states (flat/raise on other sets) need a stated choice in build.md.

HTML stages: if Reset hides what the reveal names, re-show the inspected state when phase === "reveal" (and disable Reset then); a hook blocks any Bash command that touches a protected path, even a grep, so read src/kit with Grep/Read.

Revise v2: cut the unsourced cat clause and its claim c4, made the recall a circle (round tank) so c2 covers it, reset c1-c3 to unverified; meta check --order looks for *.test.mjs and reports a fail for lesson orders, so use npm run check + tsc instead
Check illustrative comparisons against real measurements: a crouching cat (about 19.6 cm, Pongrácz 2024) is taller than the 15.9 cm rope gap.
When the stage says "tilt any way", check the bound over all angles, not just the preset ones: for 2,3,6 the circles about the hinges are 1 cm apart.
When a stage limits the possible values (two backs per card), enumerate the full space too, so the claim does not rest on the simplification.
Review files are append-only and the claims guard reads the status words in each table row: on a re-check write a new file, and do not add an old-status column.
Lay-flat best case refutes the tilt misconception on screen; reveal straight-line reason carries the general case.
Tapping the tempting card (4) and seeing both backs fine is the decisive frame; reveal answers exactly the wrong pick.
Flat Earth zoom frame on the same 20 cm ruler as the ball refutes the size-dilutes-the-metre misconception on screen; reveal answers why size never enters the sum.
